At the river's edge, I suddenly saw a small snake,
and tried to pick it up and throw it into the deep water.
Because of this, in the clear pond, it learned to cultivate its nature,
and recently, it even learned to command thunder and wind.
I pitied the fish in the dry pond with little water,
so I flowed a trickle of water into the ditch.
Recently, it slightly resembled becoming scaled,
then it claimed that all the dragons were inferior.
Seeing that parrot speaking so clearly,
I spared no effort to raise it to maturity.
Recently, it knew its feathers were strong,
and constantly made complaining sounds in the air.
The hateful little shaggy dog,
I raised it, toiled, and fed it richly.
I doted on it, intending it to guard,
who knew it would turn and bark at its master?
The duckling learned to float and sink on the water,
following its nature, it had no attachment or longing.
It's a pity the hen's heart was broken,
how could it know it was an ungrateful bird?
Night after night, the spider spun much silk,
weaving webs back and forth in the air.
I thought it would stay in its old place wholeheartedly,
who knew its intention was to seek another nest?
With jade hoofs and red ears at the trough,
it was fed so well it truly became stout.
I did not expect it to be ridden or to serve as transportation,
but recently, it has become particularly difficult to ride.
Ailanthus and common trees surrounded the pavilions,
why cut them down only to replant them?
It's just a futile waste of effort,
in the end, they won't become timber for beams.
No one in the world, great or small, knows or hears,
their coming and going are more than usual, and they do not exist.
Since their foundation is base and inferior,
how can they be chosen to accompany a young lord?
After the recitation of the Rénwáng Bōrě Jīng
was concluded and the seat ascended,
first recite the gāthā,
burn incense,
and invoke the names of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Ever since the Great Awakening opened the mysterious gate,

The five sections and three vehicles, all the ocean-like treasuries,

Monks and nuns, the four assemblies, come to the golden land,

Since you are now able to leave the burning house,

The sacred teachings of the three vehicles are truly worth hearing,

Not only will Buddhahood be achieved in the future,

Day after day, you only worry about family affairs,

All of you, for a moment, join your palms,

But this humble monk, born in a degenerate age,

entirely lacking in learning and understanding,
receiving human and celestial offerings in vain.
Traveling east to the splendid capital of the Táng [Dynasty],

I intended to travel and meditate on Mount Wǔtái,

Desiring to widely propagate [the Dharma],

Bearing a staff, I came west,

making three robes in the deserts,

Personally visited Niútóu Shān,
and toured the kingdom of Yútián.
I further wished to ascend the snowy peaks in the west,

I lament my deep karmic obstacles,
and being afflicted by illness,

I behold our sagely Tiān Kèhán, the great Huíhú kingdom,

The Heavenly King's fame spreads across the four seas,

Having long received the prophecies of all Buddhas,

Having pleased the nine-five [position of honor],

His princesses, Dèng Lín and others,

Sweeping away barbarians in mountains and rivers,

Thus, Gělü and Yàomó,

All the barbarian tribes,

This truly describes their own country,

This humble monk is fortunate to be in the gate of Śākyamuni,

Officials and generals, etc.,

Good men and good women,

Whoever listens to the Dharma,

(Buddhist disciples)
Long sigh, sunk in transmigration for countless kalpas,

In the three lower realms of hell, suffering hardships,

Sins of killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct,

Frivolous talk, double-tongued speech, uttering harsh words,

Greed, hatred, wrong views, and ignorant karma,
will surely lead to the three evil paths.
Not encountering good friends to pity you,

Thrown into pots of boiling water and charcoal furnaces,

"Why did you not cultivate in your past life?

Driven up mountains of knives and trees of swords,

Iron eagles come to peck out eyes,

Black ropes, crisscrossing, nail you,

Finely pounded pepper and ginger, a bowlful,

Fearing not the hells of the future,

Cut some from your own body to eat,
then you will know if there is sin or not.
Perhaps they are various Buddhas as animals,
or perhaps Bodhisattvas who have transformed.
If one can refrain from eating the flesh of sentient beings,

The Sūtra of Amitābha Spoken by the Buddha.
Before explaining this sūtra,
I shall divide it into three sections: first, the preface;
second, the main teaching;
and finally, the circulation.
Each sentence and each verse
is worth hundreds and thousands of taels of gold.
I will meticulously explain it to the disciples.
We shall now dedicate the merits generated by expounding and praising this Mahāyāna Amitābha Sūtra,
first to adorn the Great Khān Heavenly King,
humbly wishing his life be as long as the sun and moon,

This is offered for the Great Khān Heavenly King.
(Recite all Buddhas).
To the various Heavenly Princesses,

(Recite Buddha).
To the various Heavenly Attendants,

To the various Chancellors,

To the various Dūdū, Méilù, Dágān, Shǐ, Zhuāngshǐ, Sàwēn, Dìlüè,

may everyone increase in rank and position,

May their official positions gradually rise,

To the various monastery Vinayas, Laws, Saṅgha Administrators, Dharma Masters, Vinaya Masters, all monks, nuns, and Áyíshī,
may all in the three assemblies of Lónghuā
ascend to the couch of liberation together.
In the count of the Bhadrakalpa,
may they swiftly realize the fruit of non-action.
To the various Upāsakas and Upāsikās,
humbly wishing their roots of goodness daily advance,

May their faith be unwavering,
and may they also meet the three assemblies of Lónghuā.
Furthermore, may suffering cease in the three lower realms,
and pain stop in hell.
May patients in bed

May mothers in difficult months of pregnancy

May prisoners in jail

May strangers and distant travelers

May travelers on the road

For those enslaved as servants or maids,

For those in debt or owing money,

May the deaf hear,
the mute speak,
the lame walk,
and the blind see.
Thus,
may all four hundred and four diseases
be eliminated.
May all wishes
be quickly fulfilled.
May wars not arise,
and epidemics cease.
May the five grains yield abundant harvests,

May all uphold the ten good deeds,

May all together awaken to the true vehicle,

For these reasons,
recite all Buddhas.
(Disciple of Buddha).
The merits of Mahāyāna are immeasurable,
first offering the cause and effect to the Heavenly King.
May his lifespan be extended for millions of years,

May all from the four distant reaches come to his throne,
and the seven provinces be peaceful and rejoice in the prosperous times.
In this life, may he ascend to the position of the Son of Heaven,
and in the future, surely become a King among Dharma.
Princess Dènglín is like a divine immortal,
not only mortals but even Buddhas pity her.
If you wish to know where she was born and raised,
you should know it was entirely in the Tuṣita Heaven.
Though residing in the Desire Realm, surpassing mortal status,
morning and evening, she always faces the sagely king.
May she be born with right view, eliminating wrong views,
and in the next life, swiftly sit upon a golden lotus.
I wish to further discuss names and characteristics,
but I fear wasting time.
It is better to explain the sutra text,
and quickly attain Bodhi and Buddhahood.
However, because everyone loves sounds and forms,
I skillfully employ clever words.
Do not wonder at the repeated verses,
for it is crucial that the disciples are joyful.
For instance, in the Sahā World,
one must use sounds and forms as manifested bodies.
In the upper realm, the Fragrant Abode Tathāgata
attains Buddhahood simply by smelling fragrance.
Some awaken to the path through taste,
others arouse their minds through touch.
For those of the five great vehicles,
the five sense objects all become Buddha-deeds,
and all things are fundamentally Suchness.
Just as the lotus emerges from muddy water,
vexations transform into the fruit of Bodhi.
Unlike those of the Mahāyāna who hold rigid views,
constantly giving rise to discriminating thoughts.
Unaware that the five sense objects are fundamentally empty,
they assert that they obstruct the fruit of the path.
Sounds, smells, tastes, and touches are originally empty;
empty and not empty are all empty.
The Dharma realm is originally pure,
it has nothing to do with emptiness or non-emptiness.
This Sahā World
uses sound as Buddha-deeds.
Thus, the Tathāgata manifests thirty-two characteristics,
and merely by hearing the sound of his teaching,
one attains the fruit of the path.
The Vimalakīrti Sūtra states: in the Fragrant Abode Buddha-land,
people attain Buddhahood
simply by smelling fragrance.
The Lotus Sūtra states: the joy of Dharma and meditation is a taste
when eaten,
thus knowing that taste is used as Buddha-deeds.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra states: Sudhana-śreṣṭhidāraka,
while seeking good knowledge,
encountered a courtesan.
The courtesan said to the boy: "I have a Dharma
that can liberate all sentient beings' vexations of men.
For those with light vexations, merely touching my body
attains Buddhahood;
for those with slightly heavier vexations, coming to embrace my body
and kissing me,
attains Buddhahood;
for those with extremely heavy vexations,
sleeping with me
attains the fruit of the path."
Thus,
it is known that touch is used as Buddha-deeds.
These sounds, smells, tastes, and touches,
if one awakens to their empty nature,
are not different from Suchness;
if one is deluded by their principle of emptiness,
then they are the vexations of the six dusts.
The Dharma Master will now offer a few verses of praise,
to transform people without fault.
Below, the sutra will be explained.
Will the assembly listen?
Can you?
Are you willing?
The Sūtra of Amitābha Spoken by the Buddha.
The Sanskrit word is *Mùnà*,
which in Táng means "Buddha".
Buddha means "enlightened" (覺),
and there are three types of enlightenment:
First, self-enlightenment,
which surpasses all ordinary people, who are not self-enlightened.
Second, enlightening others,
which surpasses all *Dújué* (獨覺),
who, though self-enlightened,
cannot enlighten others.
Third, perfect enlightenment,
which surpasses all *Púsà* (菩薩).
Why is this so?
Although *Púsà* cultivate the three enlightenments,
they are not yet complete.
How do we know this?
The *Jīng* (經) says that a *Shídì Púsà* (十地菩薩)
is like viewing the sun and moon through light gauze,
or like viewing the Buddha-nature through cicada silk.
Thus, we know that their enlightened nature is not yet perfect,
and their blessings and wisdom are still lacking.
Only a Buddha possesses great enlightenment,
with the three enlightenments perfectly clear,
surpassing the Three Vehicles (*Sānchéng*),
hence they are called Buddha.
Take, for example, *Shìjiā Rúlái* (釋迦如來), who, over three countless *jié*,
cultivated myriad practices
and the Six *Bōluómì* (婆羅密).
In the first *Sēngqí Jié* (僧祇劫),
he made offerings to 75,000 Buddhas,
the last *Rúlái* (如來) being named *Bǎojì* (寶髻).
In the second *Sēngqí Jié*,
he made offerings to 76,000 Buddhas,
the last *Rúlái* being named *Rándēng* (然燈).
In the third *Sēngqí Jié*,
he made offerings to 77,000 Buddhas,
the last *Rúlái* being named *Shèngguān* (勝觀).
Beyond the three countless *jié*,
he cultivated the *xiànghǎo* (相好) karma for one hundred *jié*.
The *Jīngāng Jīng* (金剛經) says: "Before *Rándēng Fó* (然燈佛),
I met 8.4 million trillion *nàyóutuó* Buddhas,
to all of whom I made offerings,
none passing by without an offering."
The *Huāyán Jīng* (花嚴經) says:
"The number of dust motes in a *chà* (刹) and thoughts in the mind can be known,
the water in the great ocean can be drunk dry,
space can be measured and the wind can be tied,
but none can fully speak of the Buddha's merits."
Sanskrit says *Āmítuó* (阿彌陁),
which in Táng means "Immeasurable Life".
It should be known that it means *Ābōluómǐduō* (阿波囉米多).
The character *Ā* (阿)
in Táng means "immeasurable" (无).
The two characters *Bōluó* (波囉)
in Táng mean "measure" (量).
The two characters *Mǐduō* (米多)
in Táng mean "life" (壽).
Sanskrit says *Sùdálà* (素怛囉),
which in Táng means "sūtra" (經),
or "thread".
The preceding phrase "Buddha said"
means that *Shìjiā Rúlái* spoke it with his golden mouth.
"Said" (説)
means that the words belong to his voice,
hence it is known that in this realm,
one awakens to the Way through sound.
"Immeasurable Life"
is a Buddha's name.
One asks, "Where
is this *Rúlái* located?"
To the west, ten *Héngshā* (恒沙) away from here,
there is a Buddha *Rúlái* like *Shìjiā*.
Ten *jié* have passed since his enlightenment,
and he sits on a lotus in that country.
Although there are sages in the ten directions,
this country is the most praiseworthy among them.
Unlike this realm with its many afflictions,
it is adorned as the abode of the Dharma King (*Fǎwáng*).
The ground is gold, the mountains are jade,
the forests are lapis lazuli, and the water is tea.
In early spring, one eats *Pínpó* (頻婆) fruit,
while here in April, one bites raw melons.
Their Pure Land people are graceful,
while the *Shìjiā* world is full of goiters.
*Pínjiā* (頻伽) and *Gòngmìng* (共命) are born in the Western Land,
but this place has always been full of old crows.
Generally, the *Mítuó Fóguó* (彌陁佛國)
is different from other heavens.
All afflictions are completely absent,
there is only listening to the *jīng* and reciting the Buddha's name.
One does not encounter birth, old age, sickness, and death,
nor the sorrow of love and separation.
Although sentient beings are born by transformation,
they are not subject to the karma of this realm.
Since there are no autumns, winters, springs, or summers,
how can one suffer from alternating cold and heat?
Every morning, palms are pressed together among the flowers,
every day *Mítuó* bestows prophecies.
The *Amituó Jīng* (Amitābha Sūtra) that has been chanted above,
in Tang speech, means "immeasurable life" (Wúliàngshòu).
This refers to the Buddha Wúliàngshòu, who, in his causal stage,
practiced myriad virtuous deeds,
the Six Pāramitās.
Upon reaching the fruit stage,
he attained immeasurable lifespan,
thus being named from his fruition.
Next, "Land of Wúliàngshòu"
is named after the transforming sovereign (Huàzhǔ).
Just as one might say "Hàn Guó" (Han Dynasty),
Hàn refers to the people,
and Guó refers to their realm;
thus, it is also named after the people.
Now, speaking of the Land of Wúliàngshòu,
it is also called the Pure Land (Jìngtǔ),
or the Land of Ultimate Bliss (Jílè Shìjiè),
or the Land of Eternal Joy (Chánglè zhī Xiāng),
or the Region of Peace and Nourishment (Ānyǎng zhī Fāng).
These are various names,
which cannot all be enumerated.
Let's first speak of the Pure Region (Jìngfāng).
Regarding the Pure Land (Jìngtǔ),
there are two kinds of purity: first, sentient purity,
second, insentient purity.
Regarding sentient purity,
there are no three evil paths (sān è dào),
no ten non-virtuous (shí shàn bùshàn) actions,
no four hundred and four diseases,
no eunuchs or hermaphrodites (huángmén èr xíng),
no vipers, snakes, scorpions, or other poisonous insects, poisonous birds, or poisonous beasts.
There are no women;
all are men.
There are no one hundred and eight afflictions (bǎi bā fánnǎo);
all share the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment (sà shí qī Pútí fēn Fǎ).
There are no Śrāvakas;
all are Bodhisattvas.
There are no born from womb, egg, or moisture;
all are born by transformation.
They are not drawn by karmic retribution (yìshú yè);
all are Bodhisattvas in their last rebirth (yīshēng bǔchù)
or tenth-stage Bodhisattvas born from lotuses.
Unlike other places where beings undergo karmic retribution,
such as worms, maggots, and Garuḍas,
who receive transformed bodies.
There are no wars,
no slaves or servants,
no deceit or oppression,
no famine,
no kings or officials.
Instead, the Buddha Wúliàngshòu is the king,
Guānyīn and Shìzhì are the prime ministers,
Yàoshàng and Yàowáng act as registrars,
and the transformed child-beings are the common people.
They do not pay taxes in grain or wheat,
nor in wine or cloth.
They merely offer flowers and incense in the morning,
and chant Brahma praises in the evening;
there are no other duties.
From this, it can be said
there are no ten sorrows or eight sufferings (shí bēi, bā kǔ),
no unpleasant things whatsoever.
There are only the Jīva-jīva birds and Kalaviṅka birds.
These birds do not receive their bodies due to karmic power;
they are all manifestations of the Buddha Wúliàngshòu's emanation,
intended to make sounds to remind beings to recollect the Buddha and the Sangha.
Or, regarding the Land of Ultimate Bliss (Jílè Shìjiè),
there are no myriad sufferings;
only the joy of the Dharma (fǎlè) is experienced,
not the impure joys of the five desires.
Or, called Eternal Joy (Chánglè),
because one eternally experiences the joy of the Dharma,
without suffering or separation,
it is called Eternal Joy.
Unlike this world,
where one sings in the early morning,
suffering comes by noon,
and one starts to cry.
Or, called the Region of Peace and Nourishment (Ānyǎng zhī Xiāng),
it is a place for peace and nurturing the spirit.
To elaborate further
might waste time.
The above comprehensively describes sentient purity.
Next, we will discuss insentient purity.
Insentient refers
to earth, water, fire, wind,
and the six sense objects (liù chén) of form, sound, smell, taste, touch, and mental objects. … …
Regarding earth purity,
the ground is made of seven treasures like gold and silver.
All the grass and trees
are fragrant flowers,
or various jewels.
There are no thorny bushes, sand, gravel, or salty earth,
no high or low places, pits, ditches, or mounds,
no mountains, rocks, streams, ravines, or canals,
no poisonous grasses, poisonous trees, or bitter ginseng.
From this, it can be said
there are no unpleasant things whatsoever,
only agreeable things like fragrant flowers and precious jewels.
Regarding water purity,
all the springs and ponds
possess eight excellent qualities,
and all grow lotuses of various colors and jewels,
as large as chariot wheels.
The pond bottoms are golden sand,
and the four sides are adorned with jeweled trees.
The waves make sounds,
all proclaiming the names of the Three Jewels.
There is no clear mud, foul stench, fish, turtles, or shrimp-like aquatic creatures.
Nor is there increase or decrease,
coldness, heat, or turbidity.
It is as clear as a mirror,
illuminating all the Devas,
and all the Sages and Worthies
unanimously praise it.
Regarding fire purity,
this refers to the internal and external fire of both sentient and insentient beings.
Regarding the internal fire of sentient beings,
the four great elements are in harmony,
without the fire of feverish diseases, sores, swellings, or afflictions,
or the fire of lustful heat and vexation.
Although sentient beings possess the four great elements,
unlike this land,
where there is increase and decrease,
causing vexation to living beings.
Regarding the external fire of insentient beings,
since this Land of Wúliàngshòu
is a Pure Land,
there are no three calamities,
nor heat of sorrow.
Unlike this land,
where the three calamities arise in due time,
seven suns appear simultaneously,
burning the desire realm and the second Dhyāna heavens,
and various hells where fire continuously rises day and night,
burning sentient beings.
From this, it can be said
there is no fire of sorrow or heat.
Regarding wind purity,
this also includes the internal and external wind of both sentient and insentient beings.
Regarding the internal wind of sentient beings,
there are no thirty-six kinds of wind and yellow diseases.
Regarding the external wind of insentient beings,
there are no swirling winds, black winds, yellow winds,
or winds that blow mountains and uproot trees.
Nor when the three calamities arise,
destroying the third Dhyāna heavens and so on.
Although the Pure Land has internal and external winds,
the internal wind nourishes sentient beings,
and the external wind causes flowers to blossom and bear fruit,
or blows through the forests,
creating elegant and harmonious sounds,
proclaiming the names of the Three Jewels
and explaining the Eightfold Path.
Earlier, regarding the purity of the six sense objects,
first, regarding form purity,
there are twenty kinds of forms.
To briefly select and distinguish them:
blue, yellow, red, and white are four kinds of colors,
and the sutra fully describes four kinds of lotuses.
Shadow, light, and brightness, these three kinds of forms, also exist.
Thus, the sutra speaks of groves of trees,
hence there are shadows.
Light: first, the Buddha's light;
second, the body light of the Sages;
third, the light of the sun and moon.
Although it is called the Pure Land,
there are also sun and moon.
Unlike other heavens,
whose body light illuminates themselves,
thus having no sun or moon.
How do we know there are sun and moon in the Pure Land?
The sutra says: "Early in the morning,
they hold myriad wondrous flowers to make offerings to countless Buddhas in the ten directions,
and by mealtime,
they return to their homeland."
The sutra mentions "early morning" and "mealtime,"
thus we know there are sun and moon.
If there were no sun and moon,
there would be darkness.
Why is this so?
One sun and one moon
illuminate the four continents (Sì tiānxià),
thus there are day and night.
It is impossible for one sun and one moon
to remain constantly above the Pure Land
without moving;
there is no such principle.
Alternatively, if it is said that the Buddha's divine power
causes light to shine without darkness,
then that would be reasonable.
Smoke, clouds, dust, and mist—
these four kinds of forms should not exist in the Pure Land.
How do we know this?

Sūtra: “Beating drums to issue a decree,
seeking the Dharma in all directions,
who can for me
expound the Mahāyāna?
I shall, my whole life,
serve and attend.”
The Great King said: “The King has a private vow,
to seek the sūtra tirelessly.”
Hearing the Buddha’s name, he received and upheld it,
obtained the Líanjīng and recited it.
Then he ascended the tall building,
striking its bell and drum.
The bell sound roared, heard by all,
the drum sound boomed, filling the road.
Amidst the sounds of bell and drum,
he uttered these words: “Who can expound the Fǎhuā Jīng?
For ten thousand kalpas and a thousand lives, I will never forsake them.”
On the tower, he struck the bell and established a dào chǎng,
burning famous incense ceaselessly six times a day.
Every day, auspicious colors filled the sky,
and at all times, good omens appeared in all directions.
Heavenly dragons frequently offered protection,
sages and worthies often praised.
All Buddhas came to encourage him,
and simultaneously released the white hair-tuft light.
Bathed in light,
his joy was immeasurable,
and his fervent heart opened even more.
When will I hear the wondrous Dharma?
When will I be free from saṃsāra?
Since the Great King’s heart is so dedicated,
the sages and worthies should all feel pity and compassion.
I wonder who can expound it for him,
what name will be called forth?
Sūtra: “At that time, there was an immortal,
who came and said to the King: ‘I possess the Mahāyāna,
named Miàofǎ Liánhuā.
If you do not disobey me,
I shall expound it for you.’”
This sūtra chant says that an immortal arrived,
asking the Great King:
“Immortals always dwell in the mountains,
exceptionally lofty and serene.
Wind blows through the bamboo groves, their rhythms matching gōng and shāng,
cranes laugh at lonely pines, their sounds harmonizing with jiǎo and zhǐ.
Flocks of wild monkeys,
babbling streams.
With a mind to dwell permanently in the forest springs,
without intention to briefly visit the imperial city.
Suddenly, he heard human speech in the air,
and saw clouds rising before his hermitage.
Pondering the reason for this arrival,
he spoke to inquire about its cause.
The air responded,
“There is no other purpose.
There is a great Cakravartin King
who seeks the Dharma, willing to abandon saṃsāra.
Since the immortal fortunately has the Líanjīng,
why not take him as a disciple?”
The Great King desired to pay homage to the immortal,
the immortal accepted him for service.
He himself lived in the mountains to practice cultivation,
not realizing that in due course he would enter the imperial capital.
In his hermitage, with nothing to do, he only recited Buddha’s name,
sometimes under the trees, he only upheld the sūtra.
Pairs of auspicious cranes added to the incense seal,
pairs of spiritual birds filled the water bottles.
Only the immortal cultivated ultimate karma,
while gods and spirits respectfully attended to him diligently.
One day,
feeling an auspicious omen,
suddenly, propitious qi arose before his hermitage.
It was said that a king sought the wondrous Dharma,
sincerely praying and clearly requesting.
The immortal asked the Great King:
That day, the immortal,
leaving the mountain wilderness,
reached the King’s city by treading on auspicious clouds,
and went to the Dragon Tower without relying on a crane’s carriage.
Without ceremony,
without attendants,
he ascended into the air alone,
and arrived beneath the palace gate,
then asked the King,
expressing his heartfelt thoughts: “Human dignity, your noble position is exalted,
wealth and honor, why abandon them?”
When the immortal intended to enter the imperial capital,
a host of auspicious clouds bore his feet as he traveled.
Sages and worthies snapped their fingers in the air to send him off,
heavenly beings offered flowers along the road to welcome him.
Before long,
he arrived at the royal palace,
where auspicious qi was dense at that moment.
The immortal saw the Great King and his heart was pleased,
the King heard of the immortal’s arrival and his intent was reverent.
“For what reason
do you renounce worldly splendor,
and insist on seeking to hear the Miàofǎhuā?
I wonder for what reason, Great King,
your heart struggles not to cling to luxury and extravagance?”
The Great King told the immortal:
“I see people today,
all day harboring anger and joy.
Each one enjoys pleasant words,
everyone worries about harsh words.
When will greed for wealth ever cease?
When can love for beauty ever stop?
With flutes and songs, and ten thousand beautiful women,
with wealth and honor, and a thousand golden-wheeled sons.
Clothing scented with perfume,
brocade curtains and jade slippers.
Men’s spirit soaring to the clouds,
women’s elegance and white teeth.
If speaking of luxury and extravagance,
who can compare to this?
Before ten days of pleasure are allowed,
it is already said that so-and-so has died.
Having never cultivated blessings in life,
after death one falls into Avīci Hell.
Eternally belonging to the underworld,
constantly suffering torments.
Or iron birds peck out marrow,
or bronze snakes devour flesh.
Evil karma manifests, bringing ten thousand deaths and ten thousand lives,
torment presses, bringing a thousand cries and a thousand tears.
Or bodies are burned in feces,
or ground and pounded in mortars.
All day long subjected to abuse,
many kinds of beatings and interrogations.
Hungry, swallowing iron balls,
thirsty, drinking molten copper.
Sword trees sharp and dense,
knife mountains towering precariously.
To escape these causes and conditions,
what method is there?
Only by listening to and receiving the Fǎhuā Jīng
can such calamities be overcome.”
Pondering the affairs of this fleeting world, truly lamentable,
wealth, luxury, and extravagance do not last long.
With intent, one only seeks to attain Buddhahood,
without mind, one does not cling to being a Cakravartin King.
Even if jewels are like mountains,
brocade and silk do not fill the halls.
When the death demon suddenly arrives,
who can replace me in the face of impermanence?
The Great King said: “Pondering thus,
I do not cling to worldly splendor,
and so I shall arrange a dào chǎng,
and invite the immortal to expound the Dharma.”
Since I have met the immortal today,
my heart shall never delay.
Vegetarian meals are ordered to be made in the kitchen,
the dào chǎng is commanded to be arranged.
Thick incense smoke forms a canopy,
the palace trees, misty, transform into spring.
Though he had not yet heard the teaching of the middle way,
the Great King was very joyful that day.
Then he bowed,
begging for compassion,
“My wish, the immortal must surely know.
If you are willing to expound the wondrous Dharma now,
I will serve as your slave without objection.”
The immortal invited the Great King to the mountain,
and then said:
“You dwell in the palace,
with flutes and pipes daily.
Since there are many alluring scenes,
worldly emotions accumulate freely.
Increasing faults,
compounding transgressions.
The Líanjīng is difficult to expound here,
Great King, you must understand this.
I reside in the mountains,
where the scenery is unparalleled.
Strange fruits all grow before my hermitage,
famous flowers all bloom on the ridge.”
“Living in the palace, the King has much joy,
and plays flutes and sings songs all day long.
Food and drink are daily meat and wine,
clothing is always pairs of brocade and silk.
If greed and attachment suddenly arise again,
then cultivation will again be delayed.
If you wish to hear the subtle and wondrous Dharma,
can you follow me to the mountains?”
The Great King was willing to go:
The King heard the words, his joy was immeasurable,
this matter deeply pleased his heart.
As long as he could hear the immortal expound the wondrous Dharma,
who would worry about enduring hunger and fasting in the mountains?
He bade farewell to his kin,
wishing to accompany him,
and his family in the palace were filled with sorrow.

xiàguān juédìng bù xiāng liú."
Dàwáng gào xiānrén yán,
jù shuō qiánshì.
"Wǒ yě bù shēng xièdài,
shū wú tuìbài zhī xīn.
Jīnzhāo cǎi guǒ lái chí,
zhǐ wèi féng yú chāshì.
Lùshàng jiàn ge shīzi,
wēidé shèn shì xīqí,
hūrán kǒu fā rén yán,
shuō què duō bān shìyì.
Dào wǒ xiānrén xiūxué,
jīnrì yǐ mǎn qiān nián,
hé wén miàofǎ zhī shí,
gù xiàn shēn lái xiāngbào."
"Fú wàng xiānrén tīng wǒ shuō,
jīnrì lái chí yǒu suǒ yīn.
Cǎi guǒ jí shuǐ què huílái,
hū xiàng dàozhōng féng měngshòu.
Xiáohǒu zhènwēi cái shǐ zhù,
cóngzī biàn jí fā rén yán.
《Miàofǎ Liánhuā》 jīnzhì wén,
shīzi kǒuzhōng qīn yín shuō.
Bù gǎn xūyán xiāng kuángwàng,
wéi yuàn xiānrén chá wǒ xīn!"
Dàngrì xiānrén shèn shì xǐyuè.
Dàngrì xiānrén,
fāyán xiānghè.
Qiān nián ér bù dàn qúláo,
yīrì xī mǎn qí gōngdé.
Wén fǎ shì shí,
gèng mò yōngduò!
Rǔ jīn yào tīng 《Fǎhuā Jīng》,
wèi wǒ xū qiú qībāozuò.
able to seek the seven treasures to make a high seat,
wishing to preach the Líanjīng, what difficulty is there?
The Great Wáng said: "When Zhèn was on the throne,
my wealth and nobility were incomparable.
Pavilions and terraces were built of agate,
steps and paths were paved with lapis lazuli.
Gold was used for beams and pillars,
white jade for rafters and columns.
Windows were adorned with crystal,
doors were made of mani-jewels.
Pearls were strung to make inner curtains,
coral was arranged to form rows of trees.
The eight treasures were like mountains throughout the year,
the seven treasures filled the treasury year-round.
At that time, if I wanted a lotus seat,
what difficulty would there be in rebuilding it daily?
But now my body lives in the mountains,
it has been a long time since I abandoned the kingdom's throne.
Where can I obtain a treasure seat for myself?
From where can Zhèn seek a lotus platform?
Immortal, I only wish you would show compassion,
and perceive my heart, which has no means to offer.
How about taking sandalwood to make a seat,
and then proclaiming the dharma?
"If it is the seven treasures of the human world,
I would only teach you that they are hard to obtain.
But can you abandon your own body,
and use it to serve as my high seat?
The Great Wáng, hearing these words at that time,
was extraordinarily joyful in his heart,
only knowing that if the Líanjīng could be preached,
what could not be achieved in this matter!
"Please, Immortal, ascend upon my back,
and preach the sūtra for me now, quickly."
The Great Wáng said to the Immortal that day: "I willingly offer my own body as a high seat,
only desiring to achieve the Buddha fruit in the future,
not shrinking from enduring hardships today.
The Immortal,
observing the Wáng's feelings,
knew that his resolve for cultivation was becoming purer.
To repay his diligent efforts of a thousand years,
he proclaimed the seven scrolls of the Fǎhuājīng for him.
After hearing the Dharma,
he wished to cultivate,
passing through three æons without pause.
Having attained Bodhi and returned to the Pure Land,
he again arose with compassion to transform sentient beings.
Transforming into three types of bodies in the Suōpó world,
he preached the three vehicles to guide them.
He waited until the roots of sentient beings were ripe,
and then again proclaimed the Middle Way Fǎhuājīng.
His intention was for those listening to the sūtra in the assembly,
to know that the Líanjīng is difficult to encounter.
He broadly spoke of the diligent efforts of many lifetimes,
seeking the wondrous Dharma without fatigue.
I sincerely advise those who listen to the Dharma today,
upon hearing the sūtra, to earnestly cultivate reverence,
not only will it multiply merits like the sands of the Gángā,
but also limitless karmic obstacles will be eliminated.
Why did the ruler earnestly plead?
To escape the cycles of rebirth for long æons.
The previous prose section is now finished,
I shall now proclaim the gāthā chant.
Sūtra: "At that time, the World-Honored One,
wishing to reiterate this meaning,
spoke in verses, saying:
I recall past kalpas,
for the sake of seeking the great Dharma,
though I was a worldly king,
I did not covet the five desires.
I struck a bell to proclaim to the four directions,
'Who possesses the great Dharma?
If someone explains it to me,
I will serve as their slave.'
This chanted sūtra text, according to Cí'ēn Shū, is divided into two gāthās for seeking the Dharma,
therefore:
The Buddha preached this sūtra on Língshān,
commanding all people to praise it highly.
This Dharma is profound and difficult to encounter,
only after cultivating for many kalpas can one hear it.
I recall in past kalpas,
I was a king seeking the wondrous Dharma.
I abandoned my kingdom and precious throne,
not coveting the five desires, wishing to cultivate.
All day I struck a bell to proclaim to the four directions,
constantly beating drums to announce to the three realms.
The incense clouds above the censer were ceaseless,
in my heart, I remembered the Fǎhuājīng.
With utmost sincerity, I pleaded to the Honored Ones of the ten directions,
'Who can proclaim the subtle Dharma?
If someone can expound the true teaching for me,
becoming their slave will not be difficult.
As long as I hear a single sūtra sentence,
abandoning this royal body is entirely easy.'
I vowed not to disobey the speaker,
to shatter my body and pulverize my bones in diligent service.
The Wáng then made this declaration,
wondering who would come to speak to him.
Below, upon hearing the Sūtra's explanation of the Teacher,
whose name will be proclaimed?
Sūtra: "At that time, there was an Āsī Xiān,
who came and said to the Great Wáng,
'I possess a subtle Dharma,
rare in the world,
if one can cultivate it,
I will preach it for you.'
The Sanskrit Āsī Xiān,
here means incomparable appearance,
because his countenance is incomparable,
and his majestic virtue is incomparable.
Cí'ēn Shū: "People, through the Dharma, have achieved virtue;
the Dharma, through people, has been widely proclaimed."
Since the Wáng sought to hear without retreating,
day and night he struck the bell and beat the drum.
He thus moved the Immortal to descend,
arriving before the Wáng and promising to preach the sūtra.
The Immortal said to the Great Wáng:
"I possess the Middle Way Líanjīng,
which should be rare in the world.
Like the Udumbara flower, it has no second kind,
difficult to encounter, difficult to meet, and difficult to hear again."
When a Cakravartin king appears in the world,
an Udumbara flower first blossoms;
when a World-Honored One appears in the world,
the Mìafǎhuā is proclaimed once.
Rare, rare is the king of all sūtras,
how can one immediately find and explain it?
If one can cultivate with diligence,
I will certainly proclaim it for you.
As the Immortal promised to explain the sūtra,
internally, one must cultivate to destroy evil karma.
The Wáng heard these words and immediately complied,
his heart filled with joy as he proclaimed.
Sūtra: "At that time, the Wáng heard the Immortal's words,
his heart filled with great joy,
and he immediately followed the Immortal,
providing all that was needed.
He gathered firewood and wild fruits,
supplying them as needed.
His heart was set on the wondrous Dharma,
his body and mind were without weariness."
This chanted sūtra text, Cí'ēn Shū categorizes as "seeking the Dharma with compliance."
Since the Wáng earnestly sought the Dharma,
the Immortal promised to proclaim it.
He exhorted him to cultivate diligently,
and the Wáng's heart was filled with joy.
He abandoned the dragon towers and phoenix palaces,
no longer residing in the royal carriage or imperial palace.
He followed the Immortal with his body,
going to the mountains to cultivate the path.
Serving him without growing weary,
his body was like a servant, what difference was there?
He let the Immortal command him,
running errands day and night.
He gathered fruits to serve as meals,
drew water to wash bowls and fill bottles.
His heart was set on the Mìafǎhuājīng,
and he grew even more reverent.
He served the Immortal for a thousand years,
not the slightest trace of a retreating or failing heart.
He cultivated diligently in the mountains,
never growing lax for the sake of the Dharma.
Every thought desired the supreme path,
every heart wished to deliver sentient beings.
For a thousand years, he toiled in the mountains,
making his body a seat to hear the Dharma.
Not for his own body's craving for the five desires,
but for all living beings, he proclaimed.
(End of preceding section))
