In a moment, it was fetched
and placed on the desk. This court
summons him to come immediately.”
The Six Cao Officials bowed,
and returned to their respective courts.
Cuī Zǐyù said to the Emperor: “These three volumes of documents on the desk
are Your Majesty’s destined lifespan
and the merits you created,
all evident within.
I now wish to examine, search, amend, and alter them for Your Majesty,
but I dare not act presumptuously.”
The Emperor said: “As you have requested,
amend and alter them for me with your full intention, according to the law.”
Cuī Zǐyù then sat down,
examined the registers.
The Emperor’s destined lifespan was about to expire.
So, based on the destined lifespan, he added to the lifespan quota,
and also noted: “Ten years as Son of Heaven,
returning again to the path of Yang.”
Cuī Zǐyù finished adding to the lifespan,
and thought to himself: “Because I was of humble official rank during my life,
if not for pursuing the Emperor here,
how would I have had the opportunity to see the Emperor’s face?
Now I must seek a proper official position.”
So, he held his *hù* and respectfully reported: “I have finished amending the documents for Your Majesty.”
The Emperor said: “How is it?
Please inform me quickly.”
Cuī Zǐyù again thought to himself: “I should not directly say that I have noted ‘X years as Son of Heaven’ and that is all.
If the Emperor does not grant my request,
I cannot wait three or five more years.
I must speak cautiously.”
Cuī Zǐyù respectfully reported: “How can a humble subject like me be so unworthy
to have Your Majesty’s sacred presence here?
But I have added to Your Majesty’s destined lifespan,
and you will gain five more years,
returning to the path of Yang.”
“If I reach Cháng’ān,
all tribute items in the world
shall be bestowed upon you.”
Cuī Zǐyù again thought to himself: “This time he promised five years,
and will bestow money and goods upon me.
If I ask for another five years,
I will certainly get a proper official position.”
So he reported again: “Because of my humble status,
I previously said that five years have been noted for your return to the path of life.
I am an intimate friend of Lǐ Gānfēng in the court.
He sent a letter with earnest instructions,
not without diligence and sincerity.
Lǐ Gānfēng and I will add five more years for Your Majesty,
totaling ten years,
for your return to Cháng’ān.”
The Emperor heard his report again,
and said to Cuī Zǐyù: “I am deeply grateful to you for repeatedly adding to my lifespan.
If I reach Cháng’ān,
all tribute money and goods in the world
shall be entirely bestowed upon you.”
Cuī Zǐyù again thought to himself: “The Emperor twice only promised me money and goods,
never mentioning an official position for Cuī Zǐyù.
This shows that the Emperor values official positions greatly.”
Seeing that the Emperor did not mention an official position,
Cuī Zǐyù thought to himself,
remaining silent for a long time.
The Emperor then asked Cuī Zǐyù: “You just reported to me
that I will return to the path of Yang.
When I arrive in Cháng’ān, I will summon you,
and you must attend court.”
Cuī Zǐyù said: “I shall attend Your Majesty’s court.”
The Emperor said: “When will you let me return?”
Cuī Zǐyù respectfully reported: “I humbly request Your Majesty to issue a document,
to serve as a record.”
The Emperor said: “When I was alive,
I never understood how to issue documents;
how can I do it now?”
Cuī Zǐyù again thought to himself: “If I don’t scare him a little,
how can I get an official position?”
Zǐyù then reported: “If Your Majesty does not issue a document,
I have a question.
If Your Majesty can answer it,
you will return to Cháng’ān;
if you cannot answer it,
you will probably not be able to return to the path of life.”
Upon hearing this, the Emperor
was extremely frightened,
and earnestly urged Cuī Zǐyù: “Please give me an easy question.
I will certainly not let you down.”
Cuī Zǐyù was eager for an official position,
so he immediately took out paper, bowed to the Emperor,
and wrote down his question: “Question: Why did Táng Tàizōng, the Son of Heaven of Dàtáng, in the seventh year of Wǔdé,
kill his brothers in the front palace
and imprison his compassionate father in the rear palace?
Answer!”
Cuī Zǐyù wrote this and gave it to the Emperor.
The Emperor took the question and read it,
greatly distressed,
as if a pestle had struck his heart.
He threw the question to the ground
and said to Zǐyù: “This question makes it impossible for me to answer!”
Zǐyù saw the Emperor was worried,
so he picked up the question,
held it, and reported: “If Your Majesty cannot answer,
may I answer on behalf of Your Majesty?”
When the Emperor heard his report,
his dragon face was greatly pleased: “As you have reported.”
Cuī Zǐyù then reported: “If I answer this question for Your Majesty,
Your Majesty must open your mouth wide.”
The Emperor said: “You answer the question for me,
and also tell me to open my mouth wide,
why?”
Zǐyù reported: “It is not that kind of opening wide.
Because I was of humble official rank during my life,
currently serving as Fǔyáng County Magistrate.
I beg Your Majesty to grant me a place at the front of the hall,
and I will be fortunate to die standing.”
The Emperor said to Zǐyù: “What official position do you want?
Why did you not say so earlier!”
He also asked: “What is your native place?”
Cuī Zǐyù respectfully reported: “I am from Púzhōu.”
The Emperor said: “I grant you the title of Púzhōu Cìshǐ concurrently with Inspector of the twenty-four prefectures of Héběi,
with your highest office reaching Yùshǐ Dàfū,
and bestow upon you a purple-gold fish purse,
and further grant you 20,000 *guàn* from the Púzhōu county treasury,
for your family’s resources.”
Cuī Zǐyù received the imperial edict granting the official position,
descended the hall, bowed and danced,
thanked the Emperor,
and then went up to the hall and sat down.
As he was about to answer the question,
a report came: “The Heavenly Talisman Emissary has arrived.”
Cuī Zǐyù asked: “Why has he come?”
The Emissary reported to the Judge: “The Judge is to be conferred the title of Púzhōu Cìshǐ concurrently with Inspector of the twenty-four prefectures of Héběi,
with his highest office reaching Yùshǐ Dàfū,
and bestowed a purple-gold fish purse,
and further granted 20,000 *guàn* from the Fǔyáng county treasury.
This is the Heavenly Talisman for Cuī Zǐyù today.”
The Emperor said: “The Heavenly Talisman knows early.
I have heard that appointments in the underworld become positions in the world of the living;
it is indeed not false.”
Cuī Zǐyù then answered the question for the Emperor.
At this time, he only used six characters to answer,
saying: “The Great Sage exterminated his clan.”
Cuī Zǐyù wrote it and showed it to the Emperor,
who was happier than usual.
Cuī Zǐyù presented it, then put it away,
and also said: “If Your Majesty reaches Cháng’ān,
you must perform meritorious deeds,
send out swift horse emissaries,
order a great amnesty throughout the world,
and at the temple on the west side of the gate street,
preach the *Dàyún Jīng*.
Your Majesty should personally contribute money
to transcribe the *Dàyún Jīng*.”
Cuī Zǐyù then, according to the Emperor’s command,
took paper and transcribed one copy according to the previous number of meritorious deeds,
handed it to the Emperor,
who received it and tucked it into his bosom.
The Emperor said to Zǐyù: “I feel a bit hungry,
how can I get food?”
Zǐyù respectfully reported: “If Your Majesty is hungry,
I shall fetch food.”

(End missing)
In the past, Yàn Zǐ of Qí was sent as an envoy to the state of Liáng.
The King of Liáng asked his attendants, “What does this person look like?”
The attendants replied, “The envoy Yàn Zǐ
is extremely ugly,
with a dark blue-black face.
Moreover, his lips do not cover his teeth,
his hair does not cover his ears,
his waist is not attached to his hips.
From his appearance,
he does not look like a complete person.”
When the King of Liáng saw Yàn Zǐ,
he ordered him to enter through a small side gate.
The King of Liáng asked, “Who are you,
entering through my dog-gate?”
Yàn Zǐ replied to the King, “If a king goes to a human’s house,
he enters through the human gate;
if you are a dog’s house,
then one enters through the dog gate.
What is there to be ashamed of?”
The King of Liáng said, “Qí has no men,
that they sent you!”
Yàn Zǐ replied, “The seventy-two ministers of Qí
are all wise and intelligent,
so they are sent to states that value wisdom and measure.
I am the least intelligent,
so I was sent to the unintelligent state.”
The King of Liáng said, “I’m not saying you’re unintelligent,
but why are you so short?”
Yàn Zǐ replied to the King, “A wútóng tree, though large, is hollow inside;
well water, though deep, has no fish;
a five-foot large snake fears a spider;
a three-inch linchpin controls a chariot wheel.
What good is being tall?
What is there to dislike about being short?”
The King of Liáng said, “I’m not saying you’re short,
but why are you so dark-skinned?”
Yàn Zǐ replied to the King, “Black
is the nature of heaven and earth.
Can the meat of a black sheep
not be eaten?
Can a black ox pulling a cart
be without strength?
Can a black dog chasing a rabbit
not catch it?
Can a black chicken crowing loudly
be without principle?
While a swan is white,
it lives in wild fields;
while a funeral carriage is white,
it always carries dead people.
Though lacquer is black, it is sought after;
though an ink stick is black, it stays by the king’s side.
When picking mulberries, the black ones are tasted first.
Compared to these words,
what good is being white!”
Yàn Zǐ further said to the King, “Though a sword is three feet long,
it can pacify the four directions;
though a qílín is small,
it is an auspicious omen for a sagely ruler;
though an arrow is small,
it can kill a fierce tiger;
a small hammer can make a big drum resonate.
Compared to these words,
what good is being big!”
The King of Liáng asked, “I'm not saying you’re short,
but who was your ancestor?”
Yàn Zǐ replied to the King, “Bodies exist for life, and life exists for tasks;
polished rice and paddy rice come from manure and earth;
brave men discuss their merits,
weak men speak of their sufferings.
Now, I am speaking with the King,
why trouble to ask about my ancestors!”
The King then asked Yàn Zǐ, “Do you know the principles of heaven and earth,
the fundamental nature of yīn and yáng?
Which is father?
Which is mother?
Which is left?
Which is right?
Which is husband?
Which is wife?
Which is exterior?
Which is interior?
From where does the wind emerge?
From where does the rain come?
From where does frost descend?
From where does dew arise?
How many myriad li separate heaven and earth?
Which is a jūnzi?
Which is a xiǎorén?”
Yàn Zǐ replied to the King, “Nine times nine is eighty-one,
these are the principles of heaven and earth;
eight times nine is seventy-two,
these are the fundamental nature of yīn and yáng.
Heaven is father,
earth is mother,
the sun is husband,
the moon is wife,
south is exterior,
north is interior,
east is left,
west is right.
Wind emerges from high mountains,
rain comes from rivers and seas,
frost descends from the clear sky,
dew arises from all grasses.
Heaven and earth are separated by ninety-nine thousand nine hundred ninety-nine myriad li.
The rich and noble are jūnzi,
the poor are xiǎorén.
One whose words are inexhaustible,
that is named Yàn Zǐ.”
Yàn Zǐ recited a poem:
Long, long ago,
in ancient times,
there was a great country,
called Jiāshī.
The people were at peace and joyful,
the five grains flourished,
the four seasons were harmonious,
without any disasters or plagues.
Its king declared, “This is my blessing,
which has brought about such
peace in the realm.”
The king's consort also said, “This is my blessing.”
The crown prince said, “This is my blessing.”
The three disputed endlessly.
The King then went to ask an immortal cultivating the Way,
to resolve his doubts.
The immortal replied, “It is not due to the King’s blessings,
nor to the blessings of the consort or the crown prince.
In that forest,
the four animals — a Jiāpílúo bird, a rabbit, a macaque, and an elephant —
formed brotherhood,
practiced benevolence and righteousness,
respected each other,
and this has brought about the current situation.”
The King then went to see,
and it was indeed as he said.
All the people in the country
knew about this matter.
How did the elephant, bird, etc.,
determine their seniority?
The bird asked the elephant, “When you first arrived at this tree,
how big was it?”
The white elephant replied, “When I arrived at the tree,
I leaned against it to scratch an itch;
the tree was just taller than me.”
Next, it asked the macaque, “When you saw the tree,
how big was it?”
The macaque replied, “I was on the tree,
grabbing its branches, leaping and jumping;
it was taller than me.”
Again, it asked the rabbit, “When you arrived at the tree,
how big was it?”
The rabbit replied, “When I arrived at the tree,
I ate its leaves,
my mouth reached the top of the tree,
its branches and leaves.”
The bird said, “In the past, I ate the fruit of this tree in the mountains,
and dropped its seeds here,
which then grew into this tree.”
Because of this tree,
the four animals mentioned above
determined their seniority.
The bird was the eldest,
the rabbit was second,
the macaque was third,
and the white elephant was the youngest.
These four animals,
due to their benevolence and righteousness,
after their deaths,
all attained rebirth in heaven.
Dì Shì and all the devas,
with one voice,
rejoiced and praised them.
At that time, the Tathāgata told the great assembly: That bird
was I;
the rabbit was Shèlì;
the macaque was Dà Mùgānlián;
the white elephant is now Ānán tuó.
The four animals practiced benevolence,
and still accumulated such vast merits,
how much more so humans,
who are not without benevolence and righteousness.
Venerable Táng Sēngtǒng praised and narrated the 'Ode to the Benevolence and Righteousness of the Four Animals',
(to cultivate filial piety as a cause in advance)
(and now attain the affinity for Buddhahood),
(the reason is as follows):
How wonderful are the four animals,
able to form good deeds.
Respecting the elder and recognizing the younger,
using the tree as an analogy.
Spreading righteousness and practicing benevolence,
with humble hearts and minds.
Moving and resting, they followed each other,
never shunning heavy burdens.
With lapels connected and sleeves attached,
Chén Léi could not compare.
Feeling the world was peaceful and tranquil,
disasters and calamities did not arise.
Wind and rain were timely,
auspicious signs were presented.
The people of Jiāshī Guó,
all rejoiced.
The holy teachings were extolled,
and all devas praised them.
Afterwards, they attained Buddhahood,
the karmic causes for blessings stemming from this.
